hook_candidates.spoken: Why do grown-up sunflowers face east?
East-facing sunflowers drew five times as many pollinating insects.
Say sunflowers follow the sun forever at a quiz night and you lose the point.
I'm turning with the sun all day. Watch.

sources.title: UC Davis News (2016), Sunflowers move by the clock: growing sunflowers begin the day facing east, swing west through the day and turn back east at night; the plant anticipates the timing and direction of dawn; they use their internal circadian clock; the east side of the stem grows faster by day, the west side at night; mature plants stop moving and settle down facing east; east-facing flowers heated up more quickly in the morning and attracted five times as many pollinating insects as flowers rotated to the west

sources.title: Atamian et al., Science 2016, Circadian regulation of sunflower heliotropism, floral orientation, and pollinator visits (PubMed abstract): young plants track the Sun from east to west during the day and reorient at night to face east in anticipation of dawn; circadian regulation of directional growth; antiphasic elongation on the east and west sides of the stem; mature plants cease movement with flower heads facing east

states.text: East by day, west by night

beats.spoken: Sunflowers don't just follow the sun. They have an inner clock. I don't.
Wait. I thought the sun drags the flower along. But no sun rope. The plant uses its internal clock. I was shocked. I stood by a sunflower. It ignored me.
How does it turn? By growing. Day: the east side of the stem grows faster. Night: the west side. Its inner clock runs the show. No hands, leaf instead.
Closer. Young sunflowers face east in the morning and swing west during the day. At night they turn back and anticipate dawn. Scientists call it heliotropism. I call it showing off.
Grown-up sunflowers stop, facing east. East-facing flowers warmed up faster in the morning and drew five times as many pollinating insects as ones turned west. I face east too. No bees.
Remember: young sunflowers turn by their inner clock, grown-ups face east. Right, my turn. I spin along. Result: heading unknown. I guess I over-spun.
I'll just lie here for a bit. More Zonkfruit? Follow the channel. I'll get up in a minute.
